decisions.decision: Briarwake is the public name. The prior Source/Briarwake naming proposal was not a verified game-repository rename; use the existing RPG physical identifiers under ADR-011.
decisions.historical_decision: Briarwake name and Source/Briarwake paths supersede tentative RPG naming.
decisions.status: Physical-path assumption superseded by ADR-011; public branding retained

decisions.decision: Slice B checkpoint after phase 19, because Wayfinder cartography appears at 19.
Minimal NPC supply service at 13 and durable project board at 15; extend same owners at 22/23/25.
Basic ability fixture at 09; full combat discipline definitions at 12.
Partial guide and provisional register until missing source audits and full editorial/implementation details are completed.

Committed requirement: every new character selects permanent FactionId and CombatDisciplineId plus one changeable active VocationId. Retain UCombatDisciplineDefinition and the existing VocationId/Progression/Revision owners. Combat XP/talents and keyed vocation XP/mastery/skills/recipes/techniques/accomplishments are independent; a never-trained vocation starts at Level 1 and returning restores its saved progression without rewards replay. Inactive specialist permissions are disabled. Preserve the existing provisional trainer restrictions; do not add class changes or cross-identity filters. Supersedes ambiguous creator/progression wording, not the preserved master prompt. At that audited baseline faction content was unresolved. ADR-007 now supplies the authored catalog/contract without changing this class/vocation policy. Executable faction integration remains an unresolved integration dependency in Briarwake.

Committed faction taxonomy: four permanent political allegiances use data IDs; Hearthward-only desired MVP selection, three locked future definitions, Hollow Covenant nonplayable and three preserved independent civic organizations. Runtime files remain prohibited by AGENTS; authored contracts/content/test models are not a game implementation. ADR-006 class/vocation requirements are unchanged.

Faction full slice first at Phase26 after existing owners/resources/NPC assistance; preserve Phases00–31, baseline NPC13, project15 and SliceB19. Phase05 registers definitions/disposable creator fixture only; definition activation is not production selection readiness.

Proposed schema3 adds faction version/standings and explicit recovery atop schema2; unknown old-save population means no silent faction default. Canonical North Road ID project.elderwood.north-road retains NorthRoad storage key and documented project.north-road legacy alias; normalize before source uniqueness, never create two projects.

PvE-first rivalry uses bounded NPC policies and optional versioned crossing consultation, not player combat. One account ballot per fixed round, majority, tie/empty shared-passage; public reversible results never rewrite personal branches, construction or essential solo access. Existing neutral social/economy rules retained.

Briarwake is an original 2D pixel-art fantasy MMORPG being developed from the ground up in Unreal Engine 5.8.3. The existing Briarwake Unreal repository is the development starting point. No previous game implementation, port or conversion is required. Earlier game_docs material is optional historical and engineering reference. Each phase introduces or extends Briarwake’s own systems; planned contracts are not runtime evidence. Briarwake is the public game name; RPG is the verified physical project and runtime module identifier. Open RPG.uproject and use Source/RPG/RPG.Build.cs, Source/RPG.Target.cs and Source/RPGEditor.Target.cs. Keep Content/Game/, existing classes, targets and configured assets intact. Do not create a second project or require a rename. Keep stable documentation asset IDs and URLs. Phase 00 verifies the existing module; later native classes use Source/RPG. Preserve within-Briarwake record/schema migrations and fenced zone transfers. No gameplay design, phase ordering, game file or historical master prompt is changed.
